records.title: LLM Teams: Harnessing Large Language Models as Multi-Agent Teammates for Joint Problem-Solving
records.rationale: The multi-agent LLM teammates here serve a computing-education leadership simulation rather than any software engineering activity, and no single- versus multi-agent comparison or failure-mode analysis is offered; useful only as background on role-based LLM teaming.

records.title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Software Engineering: Literature Review, Vision, and the Road Ahead
records.rationale: A review of LLM-as-a-judge specifically for SE artifacts supplies the verification and measurement instrumentation that RQ3 asks about, but it evaluates artifacts rather than comparing agent topologies.

records.title: MAVE: An Augmented Multi-agent LLM System for Interactive Design and Robotic Fabrication
records.rationale: MAVE is an LLM multi-agent architecture applied to AR-mediated design and robotic fabrication, outside the SE activity set, and its contribution is grounding user intent in a physical workflow rather than agent-topology performance.

records.title: Analysis Of Linguistic Stereotypes in Single and Multi-Agent Generative AI Architectures
records.rationale: This explicitly contrasts single-agent against multi-agent generative architectures, which the protocol admits in any domain, but the measured outcome is dialect-triggered stereotype bias rather than task performance or coordination reliability.

records.title: TestAgent: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Repository-Level Unit Test Generation
records.rationale: A named multi-agent framework for repository-level unit test generation that is motivated by the limited context and rigid workflows of existing single-agent LLM test tools, putting it directly on RQ2's specialization-versus-monolith question in a verification task.

records.title: VTR-LLM: Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Automated Debugging of FPGA CAD Flows
records.rationale: Named multi-agent debugging architecture for a complex toolchain; the debugging and configuration-failure setting transfers methodologically, but the FPGA CAD domain is adjacent to rather than inside the SE activities the RQs target.

records.title: MAS-SRE: A Multi-Agent System for Security Requirements Engineering
records.rationale: Applies a named multi-agent system to standards-grounded security requirements derivation, contributing a role-specialized architecture for an in-scope SE activity, though the abstract signals no single-agent baseline comparison.

records.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Design Space Exploration in Autonomous Driving Systems
records.rationale: Design space exploration over hardware/software configurations is a design activity and the paper names a multi-agent LLM framework for it, but the evaluation target is ADS configuration quality rather than agent-topology tradeoffs.

records.title: Transforming Software Development: A Study on the Integration of Multi-Agent Systems and Large Language Models for Automatic Code Generation
records.rationale: Only venue metadata was retrieved, but the title is unambiguous: a study of MAS-plus-LLM integration for automatic code generation sits squarely on RQ1 and RQ2 and needs full text to extract its comparative claims.

records.title: Envisioning Intelligent Requirements Engineering via Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration
records.rationale: An ASE vision paper proposing knowledge-guided multi-agent collaboration for requirements engineering; it contributes an architectural proposal and research agenda for an in-scope SE phase without empirical single-versus-multi evidence.

records.title: LLMPathy: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach for Eliciting Inclusive Security Requirements
records.rationale: Named multi-agent LLM approach for eliciting inclusive security requirements, an in-scope requirements activity; the workshop format and absent abstract suggest an architecture contribution rather than a comparative study.

records.title: Towards Scenario-Driven Reference Architecture for Integrating Microservices and LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: Proposes a reference architecture for embedding LLM multi-agent systems into microservice landscapes, which supplies architectural vocabulary for the design and operations side of RQ1 without measuring agent-count effects.

records.title: Efficiency-First Design for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: A Framework and Empirical Analysis
records.rationale: The snippet frames the move from single-agent tools to specialized multi-agent systems and argues that missing efficiency measures make cross-system comparison impossible, hitting RQ1's sustainability strand and RQ2's overhead-driven underperformance case directly.

records.title: Hallucination to Consensus: Multi-Agent LLMs for End-to-End JUnit Test Generation
records.rationale: Targets hallucination as the failure mode and consensus among agents as the mitigation for end-to-end JUnit generation, combining an SE verification task with an explicit reliability mechanism relevant to RQ3.

records.title: Building Agentic AI Systems with LangGraph: From LLM Pipelines to Multi-Agent Decision Workflows
records.rationale: Reads as an overview of agentic capabilities and LangGraph-based multi-agent workflow construction; helpful for orchestration terminology but it presents no evaluation, benchmark, or failure analysis to synthesize.

records.title: Multi-LLM Persona Generation for Virtual Focus Groups in Software Engineering: A Controlled, Multi-domain Study of Emotional Requirements Elicitation
records.rationale: A controlled multi-domain study using multiple LLM personas for emotional requirements elicitation gives empirical evidence on role-differentiated agents in an SE requirements task, though the contrast is persona configurations rather than single versus multi-agent orchestration.

records.title: Towards AI as a Collaborative Partner: A Taxonomy of AI Agent Behavior in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Addresses the missing definition and measurement of success as LLMs shift from one-shot generators to agentic SE partners, giving RQ3 a behavioral taxonomy and measurement framing rather than comparative results.

records.title: An Empirical Study of Waterfall-style Multi-Agent Workflows for Class-Level Code Generation
records.rationale: Explicitly criticizes prior evaluation of isolated single-agent generation and empirically studies staged multi-agent workflows for class-level code with maintainability and structure outcomes, making it a direct RQ2 comparison despite its low rank.

records.title: Complexity-Ranked Iterative Refactoring from Microservices to LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: Documents an iterative migration method from deterministic microservices to LLM agent orchestration, contributing a refactoring procedure and a candid view of the determinism loss that accompanies agentic transition.

records.title: LLM experiments with simulation: Large Language Model Multi-Agent System for Simulation Model Parametrization in Digital Twins
records.rationale: Applies an LLM multi-agent system to digital-twin simulation model parametrization in a manufacturing automation setting, which lies outside the SE activity set and offers no agent-topology comparison despite being well cited.

records.title: AgentTCP: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Change-Aware Test Case Prioritization
records.rationale: Named collaborative multi-agent framework for change-aware test case prioritization, an in-scope testing activity; with only venue metadata available it reads as an architecture-plus-benchmark contribution rather than a single-versus-multi study.

records.title: Multi-Agent Software Development for Automotive Model-Based Graphical Programming
records.rationale: Extends multi-agent software development into model-based graphical programming for automotive systems, a useful specialization case for RQ1's scope even though the journal metadata gives no comparative or failure-mode signal.

records.title: Trust-Aware Multi-Agent Traceability: Confidence-Calibrated Knowledge Graphs for Consistent Software Artifact Management
records.rationale: Confidence calibration over a traceability knowledge graph is a concrete verification and trust mechanism for multi-agent artifact management, contributing a measurable reliability technique to RQ3 without benchmarking agent counts.

records.title: AgentDroid: A Multi-Agent Tool for Detecting Fraudulent Android Applications
records.rationale: An ASE-published named multi-agent tool for analyzing Android applications shows role decomposition applied to software analysis and security screening, but the abstract metadata gives no single-agent baseline or coordination-failure discussion.

records.title: A Characterization Study of Bugs in LLM Agent Workflow Orchestration Frameworks
records.rationale: A characterization of defects in the orchestration frameworks that implement agent workflows is exactly the reliability and coordination failure-mode evidence RQ3 requires, and its empirical bug taxonomy warrants full-text extraction.

records.title: Requirements Development and Formalization for Reliable Code Generation: A Multi-Agent Vision
records.rationale: Links requirements formalization to code-generation reliability through a multi-agent vision, offering a verification-oriented pipeline proposal for RQ3 but presenting a research direction rather than measured outcomes.

records.title: Knowledge Assistant for Joint Utility: A Multi-Agent LLM-Driven Conversational System for Automated Task Execution
records.rationale: A conversational multi-agent assistant for general automated task execution; the application is knowledge assistance rather than a software engineering activity, and no comparative or reliability analysis is indicated.

records.title: MUARF: Leveraging Multi-Agent Workflows for Automated Code Refactoring
records.rationale: Named multi-agent workflow for automated refactoring, an in-scope maintenance activity; the ICSE companion format suggests a tool or short empirical report that supplies an architecture rather than a topology comparison.

records.title: DramaGAT: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Long-Form Script Generation
records.rationale: Long-form dramatic script generation is a creative writing task with no software engineering activity, and the abstract metadata shows no single-agent comparison or generalizable coordination failure analysis to justify retention.

records.title: A Research Roadmap for Augmenting Software Engineering Processes and Software Products with Generative AI
records.rationale: A design-science research roadmap for GenAI across SE processes and products feeds RQ1's future-work strand and helps position agentic approaches within the broader agenda, but it is not itself a multi-agent study.

records.title: Mitigating Cognitive Vulnerabilities in Code Generation via Multi-Agent Adversarial Debate
records.rationale: Argues that the monolithic, correlation-driven single LLM is systematically biased and uses adversarial multi-agent debate as the remedy for code generation, which is precisely the mechanism-level answer RQ2 seeks for when specialization helps.

records.title: Reducing Cost of LLM Agents with Trajectory Reduction
records.rationale: Quantifies and reduces the growing input-token cost of multi-turn LLM agent systems on SE tasks, supplying the efficiency and sustainability accounting that RQ1 needs when weighing added agents and turns.

records.title: Bugs in Modern LLM Agent Frameworks: An Empirical Study
records.rationale: An empirical bug study of the frameworks handling lifecycle execution and multiagent coordination gives measured, categorized coordination and reliability failures, answering RQ3 head-on.
